$comment: Auto-generated by alef -- do not edit by hand. Regenerated by `alef e2e init`.
title: Alef E2E Test Fixture
description: Schema for alef e2e test fixture files. Each file contains either a single fixture object or an array of fixtures.

id.description: Unique snake_case identifier used as the test function name

category.description: Test category. Defaults to parent directory name if omitted

setup.description: Setup calls executed before the main call

call.description: Named call config to use. References [e2e.calls.<name>]. Defaults to [e2e.call] when omitted

input.description: Input data passed to the function under test. Fields map to args via [e2e.call.args] config

preserve_input_urls.description: Pass this fixture's declared URLs to the call verbatim instead of substituting the mock server address. mock_url and mock_url_list args otherwise ignore input.url/input.urls entirely, which silently rewrites the subject of any test whose point is the address itself (SSRF policy, scheme rejection, host parsing). Opt in per fixture; there is deliberately no absolute-URL heuristic

config.description: Optional fixture-level config mirrored into input.config before code generation

visitor.description: Visitor callback specification for visitor-pattern tests

args.description: Fixture-level argument mappings. When present, overrides the resolved call args

assertion_recipes.description: Assertion recipes enabled for domain-shaped assertion shortcuts and streaming pseudo-fields. `mock_requests` (alef issue #433) gates every `mock.*` field on the `assertion.field` schema: it must be a deliberate opt-in because the capture injects an HTTP round trip into the mock server for every test that asserts it.

assertions.description: List of assertions to check on the result

docs_client.description: How the documentation snippet constructs its client. Docs-only: it never affects the generated e2e suite, whose client must keep pointing at the mock server.

base_url.description: Base URL the snippet's client is constructed with. Each binding wraps it in its own optional syntax.

args.description: Verbatim argument expressions following the base URL, keyed by binding language (rust, java, ...). Overrides client_factory_trailing_args for this fixture only.

mock_response.description:
Mock HTTP response for testing HTTP clients. The mock server also exposes a request-count introspection API for `mock.*` assertions (alef issue #433): `GET /__alef/requests/total?prefix=

` and `GET /__alef/requests/one?key=%20`, each returning a bare, plain-text decimal integer body.

body.description: Response body. Accepts four host-substitution tokens the mock server replaces before responding, so a fixture can exercise a multi-host call (SSRF policy, redirect targets, cross-origin checks) without hardcoding an address the mock server did not actually bind: `{{mock_origin}}` (the fixture's own mock server origin), `{{mock_alt_origin}}` (a second, distinct origin), `{{mock_sub_origin}}` (a subdomain of the primary origin), `{{mock_foreign_origin}}` (an origin unrelated to the primary one).

languages.description: Languages to skip. Empty array means skip all

field.description: Dot-separated field path on the result object. Also accepts the `mock.*` request-count virtual-field namespace (alef issue #433), which asserts against the generated mock HTTP server's own request log rather than a field of any result type: `mock.requests.total` (every request the mock server has recorded) or `mock.requests["<key>"]`, where `<key>` is either `"<METHOD> <path>"` (e.g. `"POST /v1/chat"`) or `"<path>"` alone (any method, e.g. `"/v1/chat"`). Every existing assertion type that operates on an integer (`equals`, `greater_than_or_equal`, `count_min`, ...) works against it unchanged. Requires the `mock_requests` recipe in `assertion_recipes` -- see that property's description.

value.description: Expected value (type depends on assertion type)

method.description: Method name to call on the result

check.description: Assertion check type for the method result (equals, is_true, is_false, greater_than_or_equal, count_min)

args.description: Arguments to pass to the method call

return_type.description: Return type hint for generated assertion code

skip.description: Explicit acknowledgement that this assertion cannot be generated. An assertion whose field does not resolve fails generation by default; declaring it here is the only way to keep such an assertion, and the skip is still counted -- bucketed by `kind` -- in the end-of-run summary. Use `true` for every language, or an object to scope it.

languages.description: Languages this assertion is skipped for (empty means all)

kind.description: Which backlog this skip belongs to. `not_representable`: alef cannot express this assertion shape yet -- an assertion *kind* such as "the call returned an error", a property of the call rather than the result, or an assertion over a stream's event sequence. `language_limitation`: the target language, ABI or binding genuinely cannot reach the field.

reason.description: Why this assertion cannot be expressed here
